heading: THE HARMS OF SHORT-FORM VIDEO ON THE BRAIN ARE STARTING TO SHOW (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: A researcher and journalist examines emerging evidence that short-form video content is causing measurable cognitive harm, particularly to attention, impulse control, and memory formation in young adults and teenagers. A 2026 meta-analysis of roughly 70 studies published in Psychological Bulletin found associations between short-form video use and negative cognitive changes that were stronger than associations with mental health problems, with the strongest relationships observed in attention and impulse control, though research on other cognitive domains remains sparse. The author's own research found that increased phone use correlated with worse working memory performance, and uncontrolled short-form video use predicted weaker episodic memory—the ability to remember one's own life experiences and construct a sense of self. Tech executives like Mark Zuckerberg argue the science isn't settled, but Meta has agreed to a $17 billion settlement requiring design changes for young users, including a two-hour daily cap and nighttime lockouts, implicitly acknowledging that short-form video and passive consumption are problematic. The article argues that while litigation and science lag behind technological change, the convergence of research findings, lawsuits spanning mental health and data privacy, and user intuition suggests cognitive risks are real and affect both adolescents and adults.
strategic_hook: Understanding the cognitive and behavioral mechanisms by which short-form video drives compulsive use patterns is critical for competitors or platforms seeking to differentiate on user wellbeing and to identify unmet customer needs around control and intentional media consumption.

heading: HAS MAINSTREAM CULTURE DISAPPEARED? NEW YOUTUBE TRENDS RESEARCH SAYS NO (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: YouTube's new Culture & Trends Report, developed with NRG, reveals that mainstream culture hasn't disappeared but has fundamentally shifted in meaning. The research surveyed thousands of people aged 14-44 and found that while audiences now consume highly personalized content through fragmented digital communities, shared cultural moments still break through—63% of younger respondents feel part of something bigger when they share interests with others. The report identifies three signals that define modern mainstream: visibility (repeated exposure across platforms), comprehension (shared understanding requiring no explanation), and participation (active engagement like commenting, creating, and remixing). Digital creators and memes now rank as culturally significant as traditional celebrities and major events, with YouTube creators at 77% awareness and memes at 78%, nearly matching Hollywood celebrities at 79%. A key example is "The Backrooms," which evolved from a niche internet concept into fan-created content that garnered 90 million views and eventually became an A24 theatrical release earning $118 million globally. The research shows that younger audiences increasingly view creator success as their own achievement, with 60% feeling they actively helped build that success.
strategic_hook: This research directly supports customer strategy work by mapping how modern audiences discover, validate, and engage with cultural content—critical insights for understanding customer needs and journey mapping in platform design, content recommendation systems, or entertainment marketing strategies.

heading: "PROOF OF HUMANITY" IS THE BIGGEST MARKETING OPPORTUNITY RIGHT NOW (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article argues that "proof of humanity" has become a major marketing opportunity as customers increasingly reject AI in favor of genuine human interaction. A Gartner survey found 53% of customers would consider switching providers if they discovered AI in customer service, while 66% of people under 30 react negatively to AI in advertising. Companies like Aerie (which pledged never to use AI-generated people in ads), Port (which labels its chat widget as handled by a human), and Ramp (which put an actor doing expense reports by hand in a Manhattan window for 85 million views) are capitalizing on this trend. The article outlines three practical strategies: change chat interfaces to emphasize human support with names and photos, make explicit anti-AI pledges in marketing, and create in-person experiences like pop-up cafés or phone-free zones where customers meet real employees or engage without technology.
strategic_hook: Understanding that customer sentiment has fundamentally shifted against AI automation in customer-facing functions is critical for developing competitive positioning and messaging strategy that resonates with current buyer preferences.

summary: This article announces a webinar featuring Rachel Duffy, Head of Community at The Times and Sunday Times, discussing Reddit strategy for major media brands and companies. Duffy has built Reddit relationships for The Times by working directly with moderators, understanding subreddit culture, and treating the platform as a community engagement channel rather than a broadcast medium. The webinar covers Reddit fundamentals, how to develop a Reddit strategy from scratch, measurable wins in brand visibility and traffic, and the evolving role of Reddit as search and AI change audience behavior. The event is hosted by Standing on Giants, a community strategy consultancy that has worked with brands like Airbnb, Lenovo and Sonos, and emphasizes the importance of slow, relationship-based community building over direct brand promotion.

heading: DOES RETAIL MEDIA ADD VALUE? (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: Retail media—advertising sold by retailers like Amazon—generates a $140 billion global market with U.S. spending projected to reach $69.33 billion in 2026, a 17.9% increase. The core question is whether retail media creates genuine value or simply shifts margins. For advertisers, value exists only when campaigns generate profitable incremental sales that wouldn't have occurred otherwise; a $1,000 ad spend creating $5,000 in new sales with $1,500 contribution margin yields $500 in net benefit, but the same $1,000 spend on a sale that would have happened anyway represents pure margin erosion. For retailer-publishers, prominent ad placements can similarly cannibalize organic conversions, as when a $3,000 monthly sponsorship displaces enough natural sales to reduce overall margin rather than increase it. The article argues that return on ad spend alone cannot justify retail media investment; instead, both advertisers and publishers must measure incremental impact through randomized experiments, marketing mix models, or simpler methods like tracking new-customer sales and organic performance trends.
strategic_hook: Companies evaluating retail media investments need customer-journey research to distinguish between incremental demand creation and cannibalization of existing conversions, which determines whether the channel actually improves business economics.

heading: ARE YOU DOING MARKETING…OR BUILDING SOFTWARE? (7 MINUTE READ)
summary: Marketing teams are conflating marketing work with software development by jumping directly into building AI automations in-house without first sorting which work should come from vendor tools, external experts, or internal builds. MIT research shows that 95% of enterprise AI projects fail, with internal development efforts having substantially lower success rates than external partnerships, yet organizations continue to favor building over buying despite the cost. The article argues that teams should spend just 30 minutes sorting AI work into three categories—vendor software, expert consulting, or in-house builds—before proceeding, because skipping this step leads to expensive mistakes like building 15-step workflows with no documentation or tests instead of automatable single-step tasks. The core insight is that tools don't eliminate the need for human judgment; outputs still require verification by someone with subject-matter expertise, meaning the skill requirement hasn't been removed, just the format has changed. Teams should buy vendor solutions for common problems (like rank tracking or brand monitoring), contract out workflows they've never built before, and reserve in-house automation for truly custom workflows their team understands deeply, marked with clear inputs, outputs, and verification checks.
strategic_hook: Understanding which marketing processes are truly differentiated versus commoditized—a market analysis question—is essential to building a sound business case for AI tool investments versus internal development, directly informing resource allocation decisions.

heading: 3 IN 4 AMERICANS USE PHONES WHILE WATCHING TV (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: Omdia research presented at IBC 2026 reveals that approximately three in four US TV viewers regularly use smartphones simultaneously while watching television, fragmenting their attention between screens. This dual-screen behavior has expanded significantly across age groups, with simultaneous media use among adults aged 55-64 rising from 42 percent in 2023 to 56 percent in 2026, and among those 45-54 increasing from 62 percent to 73 percent. The competitive landscape for television has fundamentally shifted from traditional channel and streaming service competition to competing directly with short-form and vertical video content on mobile devices. Omdia's Global Head of Media & Entertainment María Rúa Aguete framed this as an "attention problem" rather than a content problem, emphasizing that success requires understanding how audiences move between screens rather than treating TV and mobile as separate environments.
strategic_hook: Understanding how viewers distribute attention across multiple screens simultaneously is critical for developing customer journey maps that reflect actual viewing behavior and for designing advertising strategies that can compete for engagement on both the TV and mobile screens audiences use together.

heading: COMPANIES ARE HIRING EDITORS TO RUN THOUGHT LEADERSHIP AND MEASURING THEM ON PIPELINE (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: Companies are increasingly hiring senior editorial leaders to run thought leadership programs and measuring them against pipeline and revenue metrics rather than content output measures like article counts or downloads. Workato's Alex Lamascus exemplifies this shift, reporting to sales leadership rather than communications and being held accountable to win rates, deal velocity, and average sales price. According to the 2025 Edelman-LinkedIn B2B Thought Leadership Impact Report, 75% of decision-makers say thought leadership prompted them to consider new products, and 70% of C-suite executives say it has led them to reconsider current vendors. The trend reflects a move from viewing thought leadership as a campaign-based project to treating it as a permanent operating function with dedicated ownership, particularly because 71% of "hidden buyers" who influence decisions have minimal sales interaction but spend 63% of them reading thought leadership content weekly. This professionalization is driven by the recognition that sustained, recurring research programs build category ownership better than one-time reports.
strategic_hook: Understanding how senior decision-makers consume information and the channels that reach them—particularly those disconnected from sales—should directly inform your customer journey mapping and go-to-market strategy design.

heading: GEN Z ROMANTICISED THE LIBRARY INTO RELEVANCE AGAIN (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: Gen Z has driven a physical revival of public libraries through viral social media content—"come to the library with me" videos and library card posts on TikTok and Instagram—that frames libraries as sanctuary spaces rather than just book repositories. According to the American Library Association, 67 percent of Gen Z report recent library visits, driven partly by the search for a "third place" outside home and work that requires no commercial participation. Beyond books, modern libraries now offer services like podcast studios, 3D printers, and workshops, with institutions like Finland's Oodi Library leading this evolution. The data shows 85 percent of Gen Z actively seek physical spaces to unwind, and library visitors report lower loneliness metrics; notably, over half of young adults who visit libraries don't identify as active readers but use workspaces and attend community events. This digital romanticisation translates into tangible foot traffic that provides councils with patronage numbers needed to justify funding and keep these civic institutions open. Additionally, physical books have regained cultural currency among Gen Z, who purchase roughly twice as many print books as e-books monthly, and reading itself has become a status symbol.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: DON'T USE QUESTIONS IN YOUR TITLES (1 MINUTE READ)
summary: Research from Stanford University analyzed over 22,000 news articles, 3 million academic articles, and 53,000 Reddit posts, finding that titles using questions instead of statements significantly underperform. Question-formatted titles received 71.6% fewer comments, 53.7% fewer upvotes, 12.6% fewer clicks, and 4.9% fewer academic citations across three experiments. The mechanism is that audiences seek clear, certain information when deciding what to read, and questions signal uncertainty, making content appear less informative and valuable. The effect holds regardless of question type (direct, rhetorical, or open-ended) and is likely stronger in uncertainty-avoidant cultures. The recommendation is to replace question titles with assertive statement formats, exemplified by changing Zapier's "App comparisons" collection from question-based titles to formats like "X compared to Y."
strategic_hook: none.

heading: STOP TRYING TO GO VIRAL. YOU NEED THE RIGHT 100 PEOPLE TO KNOW WHO YOU ARE FIRST (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article argues that personal branding success depends not on accumulating large follower counts but on being recognized and remembered by the right 100 people in your industry. The author contends that repeated visibility among relevant people—such as hiring managers, founders, or marketing directors—creates familiarity and trust that drives real opportunities like job offers, speaking engagements, and collaborations. Rather than chasing viral content or high-volume reach, the strategy is to build positioning around a specific topic (e.g., "B2B content" or "creator marketing") and reinforce it consistently until you become the person associated with that expertise. The piece emphasizes that opportunities that appear "random" usually follow months of invisible audience-building work, and that 300 industry professionals who know exactly who you are is far more valuable than 100,000 passive followers.
strategic_hook: Understanding the job market and decision-making process of hiring managers (or other key decision-makers) should inform a customer strategy that segments which audiences matter most and what specific value proposition will resonate with them.

heading: AI OVERVIEWS AND PAID SEARCH: WHEN TO FIGHT, INFLUENCE, OR GENERATE DEMAND (7 MINUTE READ)
summary: Google's AI Overviews have fundamentally altered search economics, yet most paid search strategies still apply uniform bidding rules across all query types. The article proposes a three-bucket framework: Fight (high-intent commercial queries where winning top position above the answer justifies premium costs), Influence (informational and mid-funnel queries where the goal shifts to being cited within the answer rather than capturing clicks), and Generate Demand (zero-click queries where paid search alone cannot rebuild the funnel, requiring investment in YouTube, Demand Gen, and content instead). Practical implementation requires semantic coherence in ad groups, clean conversion tracking, and regular classification of keywords by intent type and AI Overview presence. The framework addresses three structural changes: click-through rates falling on informational queries, cost per click rising due to fewer premium positions, and position becoming harder to read below the Overview. B2B and industrial accounts especially benefit from reallocating budget across these three buckets rather than applying a single optimization rule.
strategic_hook: This framework directly supports market strategy and business case development by helping B2B companies understand how customer search behavior has fundamentally changed and where to allocate marketing budget for different stages of the customer journey.

heading: SALESFORCE AND NVIDIA'S NEW REASONING MODEL IS EVERYTHING THE AI LABS SHOULD FEAR (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: Salesforce and Nvidia unveiled Koa, a new reasoning model built on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron, designed specifically for enterprise sales, marketing, and customer support tasks. Unlike frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic that require enterprises to upload sensitive data, Koa was trained using synthetic data that mimics customer patterns, meaning no actual customer information was ingested and therefore cannot be leaked. The model addresses a key divergence between enterprise needs and what proprietary AI labs offer: task-specific capabilities rather than general-purpose reasoning, lower token consumption, better security and data compliance, and automatic routing through Salesforce's AI gateway. Koa will serve as an alternative to Claude and ChatGPT within Salesforce's Agentforce platform for handling multi-step tasks like customer service inquiries. The move signals how enterprise software companies are building their own reasoning capabilities rather than relying solely on frontier labs, though Salesforce simultaneously announced a partnership with Anthropic called Claudeforce.
strategic_hook: Understanding customer frustration with proprietary AI labs' data-handling practices and requirements for sensitive enterprise data helps identify an unmet market need that Koa directly addresses—enabling companies to build effective AI agents while maintaining complete data sovereignty and security.

heading: DOES TV ACTUALLY SUCK NOW? (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: Emily Kirkpatrick argues that television is not inherently worse now, but rather that viewers have become worse at watching it due to divided attention, decision fatigue from content glut, and declining media literacy. She contends that TV reflects its consumers' tastes and viewing habits, noting that executives have responded to fragmented attention by creating formulaic, heavily expositional content. Kirkpatrick traces the problem to broader cultural issues including poor reading comprehension among younger generations, distraction from constant phone use while watching, and the degrading effect of social media discourse that makes it impossible to simply enjoy entertainment. She concludes that if TV quality has declined, it is primarily a reflection of audience behavior and consumption patterns rather than a failure of the medium itself, suggesting viewers have the power to change this dynamic.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: THE JOB MARKET HAS BEEN CONTRACTING FOR 31 MONTHS (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: The white-collar job market, particularly in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, and platform engineering, has contracted for thirty-one consecutive months—longer than any recession in modern data—with no precedent outside an actual recession. Rather than a formal hiring freeze, companies are using a rolling deferral pattern where requisitions get repeatedly pushed to the next quarter rather than formally closed or filled, which hides the contraction inside existing teams by redistributing unfilled work across current staff. This structural pattern means there is no recovery date to watch for, since nothing was formally declared to begin with; the deferred requisitions simply keep getting redecided every quarter by budget managers. The author predicts that this deferral pattern will continue for the next twelve to twenty-four months and that professionals in these fields will increasingly pursue income outside traditional single-employer arrangements rather than wait for hiring to recover. The article argues against waiting passively for the market to reverse and instead recommends identifying what you are actually paid for, building a smaller version of that independently while still employed, and setting your own progress milestones rather than betting your planning on a recovery date that has no scheduled arrival.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: HUMANIST AI IN PRACTICE: A PUBLIC CONSULTATION ON OUR CODE OF CONDUCT FOR MAI MODELS (4 MINUTE READ)
summary: Microsoft has published a draft Code of Conduct for its MAI (Microsoft AI) models, opening it for public consultation for six weeks. The code is grounded in "humanist AI" principles—requiring that AI systems prioritize human flourishing, remain under human control, never resist shutdown, and avoid autonomously expanding their scope or hiding their reasoning. The document includes absolute constraints prohibiting use in weapons of mass harm, child safety violations, and harmful manipulation at scale, while allowing enterprise partners to configure models carefully. Microsoft developed the code through internal teams spanning responsible AI, legal, safety, and sales, supplemented by academic consultations, business partner feedback, and community panels. The company plans to review all public feedback, publish a summary of changes, and release a revised version later in 2026.

heading: AI AND GOOGLE UPDATES TO KNOW (5 MINUTE READ)
summary: Google faced multiple regulatory and competitive pressures in September 2026 that are reshaping search and AI markets. Following a €534 million EU fine for favoring its own services, Google modified European search results to prominently feature competitor price-comparison sites for hotels and flights instead of its own tools—a move Google claimed represents "the biggest reduction in quality in Google's nearly three-decade existence," though the company provided no independent testing data. Separately, 41 of the top 50 U.S. news sites experienced traffic declines from August 2025 to 2026, with Newsweek, Daily Mail, and Business Insider hit hardest, all having attributed losses to AI Overviews and AI Mode reducing click-through necessity. Google also rolled out live NFL game feeds with play-by-play timelines and fantasy sports integration, further consolidating sports content and reducing publisher traffic opportunities. Meanwhile, OpenAI restricted competitors like Adobe from advertising standalone image and audio tools on ChatGPT while launching its own competing products, and Google released a Windows desktop Gemini application deepening AI integration across workflows.
strategic_hook: Publishers and platforms must map how regulatory changes (EU Digital Markets Act) and competitive AI product launches are reshaping customer search behaviors and click economics to inform business model strategy.

heading: WHY ACTIVITY WINS CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT (4 MINUTE READ)

Customers prioritize authenticity and humor from brands, with 85% staying loyal to genuine brands and 88% growing skeptical when brands push too hard to sell. The article highlights that 65% of customers are more likely to engage with brands that motivate people to get active, positioning activity-based marketing as a differentiator that breaks through ad fatigue. Strava for Business offers Sponsored Challenges and Sponsored Segments as alternatives to traditional advertising, featuring case studies from Samsung, Chipotle, Vittel, and Salomon.
strategic_hook: Understanding that 48% of marketers now prioritize audience quality and engagement over scale when evaluating new channels reveals a fundamental shift in customer strategy that should reshape budget allocation and channel selection criteria.

heading: THE DATA CENTER WATER MYTH (3 MINUTE READ)
summary: Data centers consumed approximately 228 billion gallons of water in 2023, representing roughly 0.015% to 0.2% of total U.S. water withdrawals—far less than agriculture (43%), thermoelectric power (42%), residential lawns (which use 20x more water annually), California almonds (9-13x more), and golf courses. A viral claim that each ChatGPT query consumes a full water bottle originated from a misreading of a 2023 UC Riverside study; the actual figure is one bottle spread across 10-50 responses depending on location and timing. Researchers identified roughly 700 references to U.S. data centers in Russian, Chinese, and Iranian state media over six months, with coordinated disinformation campaigns—including fake local news domains and Facebook groups operated from Bangladesh—amplifying water-scarcity concerns to undermine U.S. AI infrastructure development. Major operators like Microsoft and Google are responding with design changes: Microsoft cut water intensity 25% and introduced zero-water cooling for new AI facilities; Google replenished over 7 billion gallons in 2025 and shifted cooling strategies after local opposition. The article argues that while water matters at the local level, national buildout constraints will be power, land, and permitting rather than water scarcity, and that durable projects will pair thoughtful water design with transparent, evidence-based community engagement.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: GRAPHIC DESIGNER ≠ ART DIRECTOR ≠ CREATIVE DIRECTOR (12 MINUTE READ)
summary: The article clarifies the distinctions between three creative roles—graphic designer, art director, and creative director—that are frequently confused in hiring and organizational structures. A graphic designer executes visual work (layouts, assets, typography) to translate an existing brief into tangible outputs; an art director ensures visual cohesion across all mediums and channels of a single project or campaign, directing the concept's look and feel; a creative director owns the strategic vision and "why" behind all creative work, setting brand point of view and often influencing product decisions themselves. The author recounts interviewing for an "Art Director" role at a startup where the founder actually needed someone to establish creative vision—a Creative Director function—but lacked the clarity to articulate this, having borrowed a job title from a template without defining the actual scope of work. The confusion stems not from dishonesty but from the fact that at small companies one person typically performs all three roles simultaneously, making the boundaries invisible until hiring forces them to become explicit. The author argues that titles matter only as signals to cross-functional stakeholders about decision rights and scope of accountability, not as ego markers; what truly matters is matching compensation and accountability to the actual work scope, whether or not the business card reflects it accurately.
strategic_hook: none.

heading: INSIDE THE CREATOR ECONOMY'S AI RECKONING (7 MINUTE READ)
summary: Creator economy professionals have shifted from viewing AI with dread to embracing it as a strategic tool, according to interviews conducted with top creators, consultants, and strategists. Figures like Kameron Buckner (founder of Social Docket), DonYé Taylor, Gigi Robinson, and others describe AI as an accelerator rather than a replacement—Robinson saves over 10 hours weekly and has increased income by 20-plus percent using AI video editing tools. However, significant challenges remain: legal frameworks lag far behind technology, brands are attempting to extract creator prompts and processes in contracts, platforms simultaneously push AI adoption while penalizing AI-generated outputs, and widespread use of identical AI tools is flattening content quality across the creator economy. The consensus across all interviewed experts is that human creativity, emotional connection, and authentic voice remain irreplaceable and are what audiences ultimately value, making AI's proper role a supporting function rather than a substitute for creator expertise.
strategic_hook: Understanding creator needs around AI adoption—including fears about legal exposure, contract negotiation leverage, competitive differentiation, and income impact—is essential for developing products or services that serve this market segment effectively.

heading: PERPLEXITY IS TURNING CREATOR MARKETING INTO A PRODUCT TEST (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: Perplexity is restructuring its creator marketing strategy to function as a product demonstration operation rather than traditional influencer sponsorships. A recently advertised creator-marketing executive role, with a budget spanning over 100 creators and millions of dollars, revealed the company's shift toward tying creator work directly to conversion metrics rather than just reach. Creators would showcase original builds and workflows using Perplexity Computer, with the reported salary range of $175,000 to $225,000 indicating the company views this as a serious operating function. The approach addresses a core challenge: many creators view AI as a threat to their livelihoods, making creator partnerships unusually vulnerable to appearing like attempts to neutralize potential critics. Perplexity's real goal appears to be product adoption in a crowded market by demonstrating credible workflows rather than securing broad brand approval. The strategic risk is that overly polished demonstrations could backfire if creators don't authentically show where AI changes creative work economics.
strategic_hook: This reveals how customer research and product testing through creator partnerships can validate whether a tool solves genuine user problems in real workflows, informing product roadmap decisions and competitive positioning in a saturated market.

heading: HOW MUCH DOES A B2B CONTENT WRITER COST IN 2026 (7 MINUTE READ)
summary: A freelance B2B content writer in the UK charges between 30p and 50p per word, £50 to £100 per hour, or £300 to £1,000 per article, with rates varying significantly by format and complexity. Day rates average £480, while specialized work like white papers can command £800 to £4,000 and LinkedIn ghostwriting runs £100 to £250 per post or £500 to £3,000 monthly. The article explains that pricing reflects not just word count but research depth, topic complexity, SEO expertise, interviews, and revision cycles—with experienced B2B writers in technical fields (finance, insurance, tech) commanding premium rates. When comparing options, a freelancer costs roughly £800 to £1,600 monthly for four articles, significantly less than agencies at £2,000 to £5,000 but more than AI tools at £20 per month, though AI-generated content requires extensive human editing and carries compliance and reputational risks. The author argues that cheap or AI-generated content ultimately costs more because it's generic, doesn't rank well, requires heavy fact-checking in regulated industries, and fails to resonate with B2B buyers who trust people over algorithms.
strategic_hook: Understanding what drives B2B content writer pricing—research requirements, topic expertise, interview work, and revision cycles—directly informs customer strategy by revealing what buyers value and are willing to pay for in business-critical content, helping companies decide whether to invest in sector-specialist writers versus generic alternatives.

heading: ECONOMISTS CONCERNED THE AI BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO BLOW (2 MINUTE READ)
summary: Capital Economics, a London-based firm, has warned that Western economies are caught in a "late-stage bubble" driven by massive misallocation of capital fueling the AI boom. Senior markets economist James Reilly surveyed eight market indicators and found most at or near critical levels historically preceding major market crashes, including surging equity and debt issuance, concentrated market-cap in a few tech stocks, and unstable expected income growth—conditions last seen before the dot-com crash. The US Federal Reserve faces a critical decision on whether to raise interest rates to cool the market; Fed chair Kevin Warsh is expected to announce a rate hike this afternoon. The situation is unusual because core CPI inflation hit a post-pandemic low in August, yet UBS expects the Fed to raise rates while lowering long-term inflation projections—something that has never happened before. A CNN analysis notes that rate hikes may cool most investments while leaving AI spending unchecked, potentially allowing the bubble to continue inflating.
strategic_hook: none.
